region.critical_area_note: SCC 14.24.080 requires critical-area review; wetland, habitat, geologic and flood provisions can require site assessment and protective areas. The County reports a July 2026 hearings-board decision against its riparian-buffer provisions and pending amendments to SCC 14.24.530. Proposed amendments are not adopted requirements. Confirm current effective rules and site-specific buffer dimensions; no fixed riparian width is assumed here.

wa-skagit-gis.citation: Skagit GIS: parcel and municipal boundaries

wa-skagit-county-source.jurisdiction: Unincorporated Skagit permit fees and review
wa-skagit-county-source.citation: Unincorporated Skagit permit fees and review
wa-skagit-county-source.excerpt: County fees separate valuation-based construction review, zoning, drainage and grading; technology charges and specialist reviews can add to the total.

wa-skagit-mount-vernon-source.jurisdiction: Mount Vernon permit fees and review
wa-skagit-mount-vernon-source.citation: Mount Vernon permit fees and review
wa-skagit-mount-vernon-source.excerpt: The city fee handout separates building and plan review charges and applies a technology fee; planning, engineering and impacts are additional.

wa-skagit-burlington-source.excerpt: The current city schedule includes building valuation fees, plan review, planning review and separate site-plan or engineering permits.

wa-skagit-sedro-woolley-source.excerpt: The adopted schedule separates building valuation charges, residential planning review and civil engineering services; impact fees are assessed separately.

wa-skagit-anacortes-source.excerpt: The July adopted schedule separates construction, site-plan, shoreline, critical-area, utility and impact charges; review type determines the applicable fee.

wa-skagit-water.excerpt: A well permit exemption does not establish legal water availability; confirm watershed restrictions and an adequate potable supply before committing to development.

wa-skagit-agriculture.excerpt: Agricultural resource zoning restricts the placement of non-agricultural buildings; the permitted building location must be reviewed before proposing a footprint.

wa-skagit-swinomish.excerpt: Reservation land status affects permitting authority; the agreement provides coordinated review for eligible fee land and recognizes exclusive tribal authority in other cases.

wa-skagit-air.jurisdiction: Northwest Clean Air Agency asbestos and demolition
wa-skagit-air.citation: Northwest Clean Air Agency asbestos and demolition
wa-skagit-air.excerpt: Demolition and asbestos work require screening against Northwest Clean Air Agency regulations; notification and survey duties depend on the structure and work.

wa-skagit-consultants.citation: Environmental consulting hourly rate and service counties
wa-skagit-consultants.excerpt: This consultant publishes an hourly environmental-services rate and expressly serves both King and Skagit counties; project hours require a separate scope.

wa-skagit-tribal-contacts.excerpt: The state publishes tribal-government contacts for consultation; affected tribes must be identified for the particular location, resources and proposed activity.

wa-skagit-critical-code.citation: SCC 14.24 — critical areas; active 2026 riparian amendment process
wa-skagit-critical-code.excerpt: SCC 14.24.080 requires critical-area review; wetland, habitat, geologic and flood provisions can require site assessment and protective areas. The County reports a July 2026 hearings-board decision against its riparian-buffer provisions and pending amendments to SCC 14.24.530. Proposed amendments are not adopted requirements. Confirm current effective rules and site-specific buffer dimensions; no fixed riparian width is assumed here.

wa-skagit-critical-review.citation: SCC 14.24.080, .230, .420 and .530 — review and site protections
wa-skagit-critical-review.excerpt: Critical-area review and site-specific assessments establish applicable wetland, geologic and habitat protections. Inventory maps alone do not establish the permitted building area.
